title: X-ray Ptychography at the Edge: Towards Real-Time Feedback for High-Speed Nanoimaging
problem: X-ray ptychography requires computationally intensive iterative reconstruction algorithms, and recent advances in data acquisition have dramatically increased data generation rates, making real-time reconstruction challenging.
motivation: High-speed X-ray ptychography experiments need real-time reconstruction feedback to enable informed experimental decision-making and adaptive imaging strategies during data acquisition.
method: X-ray ptychography requires repeating mathematical steps to rebuild detailed images from the data collected. The problem is that modern microscopes generate data much faster than traditional reconstruction methods can process it. The solution uses graphics processors—chips that excel at performing many calculations simultaneously—installed directly at the microscope instead of at a distant computer. This allows images to be reconstructed immediately as data arrives, rather than being stored and processed later.
key_novelty: Graphics processors positioned at the microscope enable real-time image reconstruction during high-speed X-ray ptychography, making autonomous experimental control possible.
contributions: Edge deployment architecture for real-time feedback
Real-time processing during continuous data acquisition
Enabling data-driven decision making during experiments
Path towards autonomous experiments at machine speeds
limitations: Specific to X-ray ptychography application; generalizability to other imaging modalities unclear; deployment and hardware constraints at beamlines not detailed.
